title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits in the 1980s continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (numbered p.700). There Grothendieck studies profinite fundamental groups attached to the moduli tower and how Galois acts on them. Several identifications below are uncertain.

**Objects.**
- M^∧ (also written M) is a profinite lattice-type module of rank 2. It carries an action of an order-3 element ρ satisfying 1+ρ+ρ²=0, so it looks like a hexagonal, Eisenstein-type lattice.
- Aff = M^∧ ⋊ (Ẑ^× × S_3) is the 'affine' group, the trivial (split) extension of Ẑ^× × S_3 by M^∧.
- G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G is another extension of O_12^* × S_3 by M (labelled (231)). It is built from generators ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2), in the style of PSL_2(Z) = Z/3 * Z/2. The meaning of O_12^* is unsure; it may be a finite unit group linked to μ_12 or (Z/12)^*.

**What the previous page established.** The diagram (242)/(242 bis) maps M_{0,3} → Aff. The map depends on choosing a point of U_∞(Q̄) over the point '-j'. From it the extension of N_2 by M^∧ is trivial, and its splittings up to M^∧-conjugacy correspond to such points.

**First paragraph.** Grothendieck wishes to prove that the homomorphism M_{0,3} → Aff is isomorphic to the homomorphism M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G of (239), via a suitable isomorphism of extensions Aff ≅ G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. This would imply that the extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G splits. He then notes the standard fact that isomorphisms of a split-type extension with Aff correspond to splittings of it.

**§120, splittings of G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G over O_12^* × S_3 by M.**
- A lift O_12^* ↪ G_{ρ,σ} already exists (refs 150, 151).
- He looks for splittings extending that lift. He reduces this to splittings of the extension induced over S_3, labelled (243): 1 → M → S^+/μ_S → (S_3)_{s_0} → 1.
- A splitting of an extension of S_3 = ⟨ρ,σ | ρ³ = σ² = 1, σρσ⁻¹ = ρ⁻¹⟩ by M amounts to choosing lifts ρ' = ξρ and σ' = ησ, with ξ, η in M, satisfying the defining relations. This is the next page's (244).
- On the next page these relations become linear conditions:
  - ρ'³ = 1 is automatic, since 1+ρ+ρ² = 0 on M.
  - σ'² = 1 forces η = bδ, with δ = λ_1 − λ_0.
  - The braid-type relation then gives conditions on (a_0, a_1, b).
- The margin correction says 'not quite': one must restrict to the S_3-splittings that commute with G_{ρ,σ}(0) ≃ O_12^*. Only then does the equivalence with splittings of the full extension hold.

**Mathematical content.** This is an explicit nonabelian/abelian 1-cocycle computation. Splittings exist iff a class in H²(S_3, M) vanishes; if they exist, they form a torsor under Z¹ (up to conjugacy, H¹), with an equivariance constraint for O_12^*. The purpose is to identify G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G with Aff, and through that to compare the 'geometric' description (points over -j) with the combinatorial group G_{ρ,σ}.
errors: The main text's 'or what amounts to the same thing, the splittings of the extension induced on S_3' is corrected by Grothendieck in the margin. It is only equivalent once one restricts to splittings of the S_3-extension that commute with the given copy of O_12^* = G_{ρ,σ}(0). The correction itself is right.

The claim 'isomorphisms of this extension with Aff correspond to splittings' holds only up to the usual identifications (fixed identifications of kernel and quotient, conjugation by M). This is implicit but standard.

ideas.what: Hope that the homomorphism M_{0,3} → Aff coincides, up to isomorphism of extensions, with M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. This would imply G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G is split.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of extensions / Galois-equivariant identification of fundamental-group quotients (anabelian, Grothendieck–Teichmüller context)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's program (Esquisse, Longue Marche); later Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura et al. for Galois actions on π1
ideas.where_published: Possibly related themes in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific statement unsure

ideas.what: Splittings of an extension of S_3 (and O_12^* × S_3) by an abelian module M, computed through lifts (ρ', σ') = (ξρ, ησ) satisfying the presentation relations, plus an equivariance condition for O_12^*.
ideas.modern_name: Splittings of group extensions / 1-cocycles, H¹ and H² of S_3 with coefficients in a lattice

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly states as a desideratum, without proving it on this page, that the map M_{0,3} → Aff is isomorphic to M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. This would identify a combinatorially defined extension (generated by ρ, σ) with the affine group arising from Galois/geometric data at the point over -j. Whether the later pages settle this is unknown from this page.
missed.quote: On aurait vraiment envie de montrer que cet homomorphisme M_{0,3} → Aff est isomorphe à l'hom. M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G de (239)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small, concrete instance of matching combinatorial models of fundamental groups (of the modular/Teichmüller tower near an elliptic point) with arithmetic data. That is relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type questions. However, it is likely a technical lemma within his notes rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly sets up a routine computation of splittings of an extension of S_3 by a lattice. The only non-routine element is a stated wish to identify two extensions inside his unpublished Longue Marche continuation. That is of interest to historians, but the content is technical and its mathematical setting is only partly decipherable.
transcription_corrections: The equation label is '(243)', not '(241)'; this follows (242 bis) on the previous page.
The last line of the main text reads roughly 'Ces scindages correspondent biunivoquement aux couples' (with 'sont' struck out), not 'On regarde les scindages correspondants'.

Margin note reads approximately: 'Pas tout à fait : il faudrait se restreindre aux scindages (S_3)_{s_0} → S^+/μ_S qui commutent à G_{ρ,σ}(0) ≃ O_12^*. On regarde les scindages ... sous-scindages ...'
The page number at top is '700'.
